statement: Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence of integers with associated $a_k\pmod{n_k}$, such that for some $\epsilon>0$ we have $n_k>(1+\epsilon)k\log k$ for all $k$. Then $\#\{ m<n_k : m\not\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i} \textrm{ for }1\leq i\leq k\}\neq o(k)$.
status: DISPROVED (LEAN) — erdosproblems.com: 'This has been solved in the negative and the proof verified in Lean.'
notes: RESOLVED IN THE NEGATIVE: formalize the negation, i.e. there exist a strictly increasing sequence n_k (k >= 1) with residues a_k mod n_k and some epsilon > 0 with n_k > (1+epsilon) k log k for all k >= 1, such that the count #{m < n_k : m is not congruent to a_i mod n_i for all 1 <= i <= k} IS o(k) (tends to 0 after dividing by k). From the site: Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] suggest this 'may have to await improvements in current sieve methods'. Note that since the kth prime is ~ k log k the lower bound n_k > (1+epsilon) k log k is best possible here. Cambie has observed that this question has a trivial negative answer, since taking n_k = 2^k and a_k = 2^{k-1} + 1 for k >= 1 implies the only m not in any congruence class is 1, so the count is actually 1!
